rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 20 November 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🔴 HKMA expects all authorized institutions to assess and, where appropriate, enhance anti-corruption practices under the new HKAB guideline, with a compliance-status report due by end-Q3 2027. Management should establish accountable ownership, evidence the assessment and sequence remediation. • 🟡 UK regulators are consulting on non-Handbook cyber-resilience guidance for UK-perimeter firms; it is not a Hong Kong requirement. Confirm UK scope and shared-service dependencies, then monitor final guidance expected in H1 2027. Hong Kong 🔴 Guideline on Corruption Prevention issued by Hong Kong Association of Banks 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261119-hkma-brdr-ef9980b664 ⏰ Deadline: End of Q3 2027 (compliance-status report to HKMA) Products: Bank-wide operations HKMA’s circular to all authorized institutions introduces HKAB’s Guideline on Corruption Prevention for Banks. HKMA expects institutions to assess their practices against the guideline, make necessary enhancements where appropriate, and report compliance status by end-Q3 2027. The circular describes the guideline as a consolidated reference that reinforces existing regulations and statutory requirements; its good practices cover governance, whistleblowing, operational controls, consequence management and training. Actions: • Within 30 days, assign accountable first-line and Compliance owners for an applicability and gap assessment, with second-line challenge. • Map relevant controls and evidence to the guideline, including risk assessment, policy, training, whistleblowing, testing, case-log and closure evidence. • Establish reporting ownership and sequence proportionate remediation ahead of the end-Q3 2027 status report. Source: Guideline on Corruption Prevention issued by Hong Kong Association of Banks SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. 🟡 GC26/9: Cyber risk and resilience management 🇬🇧 Item ID: item-20261119-global-material-incidents-enforcement-e994140b4f ⏰ Deadline: 26 February 2027 (consultation response deadline) Products: Digital services; Payments The FCA, PRA and Bank of England opened a joint consultation on non-Handbook guidance that clarifies existing UK rules rather than adding rules. The draft expects proportionate accountability, inventories of assets and third-party dependencies, layered access controls, detection, and tested response and recovery for specified UK firms. It is not a Hong Kong requirement; any relevance to Hong Kong digital or payment services is analogous and depends on UK-perimeter entities or shared-service dependencies. Source: GC26/9: Cyber risk and resilience management Watch List • Monitor HKMA communication on the format for the end-Q3 2027 compliance-status report. • Monitor publication of final FCA/PRA/Bank of England guidance, expected in the first half of 2027.
